legal_units.title: Appeal.
legal_units.text: The applicant, if aggrieved by any ruling pronounced or order passed by the Board for Advance Rulings or the Assessing Officer, on the directions of the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner, may appeal to the High Court against such ruling or order of the Board for Advance Rulings within sixty days from the date of the communication of that ruling or order, in such form and manner, as may be prescribed.
legal_units.retrieval_text: Chapter XVIII APPEALS, REVISIONS AND ALTERNATE DISPUTE RESOLUTIONS Chapter XVIII, Division D Alternate Dispute Resolutions Chapter XVIII, Division D, Subdivision 2 Advance rulings Section 389 Appeal. Section 389(1): The applicant, if aggrieved by any ruling pronounced or order passed by the Board for Advance Rulings or the Assessing Officer, on the directions of the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner, may appeal to the High Court against such ruling or order of the Board for Advance Rulings within sixty days from the date of the communication of that ruling or order, in such form and manner, as may be prescribed.
legal_units.chapter_title: APPEALS, REVISIONS AND ALTERNATE DISPUTE RESOLUTIONS

legal_units.title: Appeal.
legal_units.text: Where the High Court is satisfied, on an application made by the appellant in this behalf, that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from presenting the appeal within the period specified in sub-section (1), it may grant further period of thirty days for filing such appeal.
legal_units.retrieval_text: Chapter XVIII APPEALS, REVISIONS AND ALTERNATE DISPUTE RESOLUTIONS Chapter XVIII, Division D Alternate Dispute Resolutions Chapter XVIII, Division D, Subdivision 2 Advance rulings Section 389 Appeal. Section 389(2): Where the High Court is satisfied, on an application made by the appellant in this behalf, that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from presenting the appeal within the period specified in sub-section (1), it may grant further period of thirty days for filing such appeal.
